title: The broad sharing link — question explanation
learningObjective: Apply least-privilege and verify recipient, channel and classification before sharing
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A project teammate asks you to upload a spreadsheet containing student IDs and contact details to a folder with “Anyone with the link can view” access.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Apply least-privilege and verify recipient, channel and classification before sharing
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option A: Share only with the verified people who need it, using an approved restricted channel and minimum necessary data. Verify recipients and classification, then apply least privilege to access and content.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option B: Temporary broad exposure is still exposure; access should be appropriately restricted before sharing. Option C: Renaming does not remove sensitive content or limit access. Option D: A personal mailbox may bypass organizational controls and create a new disclosure path.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Confirm the business need and recipient list, use the approved storage service, disable public access, and set access expiry or review where supported. Share the minimum necessary data with verified recipients using access controls appropriate to its sensitivity.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Share the minimum necessary data with verified recipients using access controls appropriate to its sensitivity.

Verify recipients and classification, then apply least privilege to access and content. Option C is unsafe because Renaming does not remove sensitive content or limit access. Option D is unsafe because A personal mailbox may bypass organizational controls and create a new disclosure path. In practice: Confirm the business need and recipient list, use the approved storage service, disable public access, and set access expiry or review where supported. Key takeaway: Share the minimum necessary data with verified recipients using access controls appropriate to its sensitivity.
